content:
We need to propose a retrosynthesis route with 3 reactions for target SMILES: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1.

The guidance: three steps: (1) amide formation from carboxylic acid + amine (coupling). (2) Doebner modification: aromatic aldehyde + malonic acid -> α,β-unsaturated carboxylic acid (new alkene). (3) sulfonamide formation: amine + sulfonyl chloride.

Thus retrosynthetic direction: target -> break amide bond to give acid and amine (step 1 reversed). The amide is C(=O)N attached to aromatic ring (anilide). So disconnection: the amide carbonyl attached to aromatic ring (c3ccccc3N). The amide carbonyl is part of the α,β-unsaturated acid side chain: /C=C/C(=O)N-... So the amide carbonyl is attached to the alkene carbonyl (the acid). In forward direction, we would have carboxylic acid (α,β-unsaturated) reacting with aniline to give amide. So retrosynthesis: break amide to give α,β-unsaturated carboxylic acid (with the alkene) and aniline (c3ccccc3N). That's step 1.

Step 2: The α,β-unsaturated carboxylic acid could be formed via Doebner modification from aromatic aldehyde (maybe p-tolyl aldehyde?) and malonic acid. The side chain is attached to phenyl ring (c2ccc(... )cc2). The aldehyde would be on that phenyl ring at the position where the side chain attaches: the aromatic ring with a substituent that becomes the α,β-unsaturated acid after Doebner. So we need to identify the aldehyde precursor: the phenyl ring with a formyl group (CHO) at the position where the side chain attaches (para to something?). The side chain is /C=C/C(=O)N... attached to the phenyl ring via the alkene carbon (the β carbon). In Doebner, aldehyde + malonic acid -> α,β-unsaturated acid where the aldehyde carbon becomes the carbonyl of the acid? Actually Doebner: aromatic aldehyde + malonic acid -> cinnamic acid derivative (aryl-CH=CH-CO2H). So the aldehyde carbon becomes the carbonyl carbon of the acid? Wait: cinnamic acid is Ph-CH=CH-CO2H. Starting from benzaldehyde (Ph-CHO) + malonic acid -> Ph-CH=CH-CO2H. So the aldehyde carbon becomes the β carbon (CH) of the double bond, and the carboxyl group comes from malonic acid. So the precursor aldehyde is the phenyl ring with CHO substituent (para to something). In our target, the phenyl ring (c2ccc(... )cc2) is attached to sulfonyl group and the side chain at para position? The SMILES: c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2 attached to sulfonyl group. So the side chain is attached at position 1 of that phenyl ring (the one bearing the sulfonyl). The side chain is at para? Not needed.

Thus step 2: break the C=C double bond and carboxylic acid to give aldehyde (aryl-CHO) and malonic acid (or maybe just malonic acid as reagent). So we propose precursor: aryl aldehyde (c2ccc(C=O)cc2) attached to sulfonyl group (i.e., p-tolyl sulfonyl? Actually the sulfonyl group attaches to the first phenyl ring (c1ccc...). The sulfonyl is attached to the first phenyl (with methyl). The second phenyl (c2ccc) is attached to sulfonyl via S=O2. So the aldehyde precursor is the same second phenyl with CHO substituent, still attached to sulfonyl.

Thus step 2 precursor SMILES: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(C=O)cc2)cc1 (the sulfonyl phenyl with aldehyde). Indeed we earlier searched that.

Step 3: The sulfonamide formation: break sulfonamide bond to give sulfonyl chloride (or sulfonyl fluoride) and amine (the first phenyl with methyl). The target sulfonamide is NS(=O)(=O) attached to the first phenyl (toluene). So retrosynthesis: break N-S bond to give p-toluidine (p-methyl aniline) and sulfonyl chloride (ClSO2- attached to second phenyl). Actually sulfonyl chloride would be attached to the second phenyl (c2ccc...). So precursor: p-toluidine (Cc1ccc(N)cc1) and aryl sulfonyl chloride (ClS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(C=O)cc2). However the sulfonyl chloride is attached to the second phenyl which also has aldehyde. So we need that as a separate precursor.

Thus overall three steps:

Step 1 (retro): target -> α,β-unsaturated acid + aniline (c3ccccc3N). The acid precursor SMILES: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/CO)cc2)cc1? Wait the acid after breaking amide: we have the α,β-unsaturated acid (c2ccc(/C=C/CO)?? Actually the amide carbonyl is removed, leaving carboxylic acid: /C=C/C(=O)OH attached to phenyl. So precursor SMILES: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/CO)cc2)cc1? But the side chain after amide cleavage is /C=C/CO (carboxylic acid). So SMILES: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/CO)cc2)cc1. Let's generate: The side chain is /C=C/CO (i.e., CH=CH-COOH). So the SMILES: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/CO)cc2)cc1.

Step 2 (retro): that acid + alkene -> aldehyde + malonic acid (but we treat malonic acid as reagent, not part of route). So precursor SMILES: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(C=O)cc2)cc1 (aryl aldehyde with sulfonyl). That's step 2.

Step 3 (retro): sulfonamide formation broken: gives p-toluidine (Cc1ccc(N)cc1) and aryl sulfonyl chloride (ClS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(C=O)cc2). So we need two precursors for step 3.

Thus the route tree: root target molecule. Reaction 1 (amide formation) with template ID (maybe 401931) connecting to two children: acid precursor and aniline (c3ccccc3N). Reaction 2 (Doebner) connecting acid precursor to aldehyde precursor and malonic acid (but malonic acid not needed as leaf? Could include as reagent). Reaction 3 (sulfonamide formation) connecting aldehyde precursor to p-toluidine and sulfonyl chloride.

We need template IDs for each reaction. We have template 401931 for amide formation (looks like amide formation from acid and amine). Good.

We need template for Doebner modification (aldehyde + malonic acid -> α,β-unsaturated acid). Search for template that breaks C-C double bond and forms C-C double bond? Might be template 659569? That one is for amide formation? Actually 659569 is for amide formation? It shows O-[C;H0;D3;+0:1](=[O;D1;H0:2])-[C:3]=[C:4]>>[#7:5]-[C;H0;D3;+0:1](=[O;D1;H0:2])-[C:3]=[C:4] which is amide formation from acid and amine (same as 401931). Not Doebner.

We need a template for aldehyde + malonic acid -> unsaturated acid. Could search for functional groups broken: aldehydes, formed: C-C double bonds, aliphatic carboxylic acid. We attempted earlier but got error due to "aliphatic carboxylic acid" is valid. Let's try again with correct list: broken: ["aldehydes"], formed: ["C-C double bonds", "aliphatic carboxylic acid"]. That we did and got empty. Maybe there is no template. Could use a generic condensation template? Might not be needed; we can still propose route using known reaction but not need to fetch template ID? The answer requires JSON with template_id numbers. We need to find appropriate template IDs.

Search for templates where functional_groups_broken includes "aldehydes" and functional_groups_formed includes "C-C double bonds". Let's try again with only those two.
